title: 05.12.26 Public Hearing - Chipman/Stake Center Annexation
agenda_text:
Public Hearing Notice - Chipman/Stake Center Annexation
Notice is hereby given that a petition for annexation was filed with American Fork City. The petition, which was accepted by the city council on October 22, 2024, covers approximately 24 acres consisting of property located at approximately 515 South 100 West.  The city recorder certified the petition, and the legislative body provided notice according to Utah Code 10-2-406. A 30-day period was allowed to give property owners and affected entities the opportunity to submit written protests. A public hearing was previously held on February 25, 2025.
A public hearing will be held on Tuesday, May 12, at 7 p.m. at the American Fork City Hall (31 N. Church Street) to allow the public to comment on the Chipman/Stake Center Annexation. After the public hearing, American Fork City may choose to deny or grant the petition and annex the area described in the petition. 
The complete annexation petition is available for inspection and copying at the American Fork City Recorder's office (51 E. Main Street, American Fork) or by emailing tlurker@americanfork.gov
Dated this 30th day of April 2026.
/s/ Terilyn Lurker, City Recorder

NOTICE OF PROPOSED TAX INCREASE
CITY OF DRAPER/SALT LAKE COUNTY

The CITY OF DRAPER is proposing to increase its property tax revenue.

The CITY OF DRAPER tax on a $941,000 residence would increase from $466.83 to $583.80, which is $116.97 per year.

NOTICE OF PROPOSED TAX INCREASE 
EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY

The EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY is proposing to increase its property tax revenue. 

The EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY tax on a $488,000 residence would increase from
$142.25 to $456.28, which is $314.03 per year.

The EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY tax on a $488,000 business would increase from
$258.64 to $829.60, which is $570.96 per year.

If the proposed budget is approved, EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY would receive an additional $6,742,938 in property tax revenue per year as a result of the tax increase. If the proposed budget is approved, EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY would increase its property tax budgeted revenue by 220.88% above last year's property tax budgeted revenue excluding eligible new growth.

The EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY invites all concerned citizens to a public hearing for the purpose of hearing comments regarding the proposed tax increase and to explain the reasons for the proposed tax increase. You have the option to attend or participate in the public hearing in person or virtually.


PUBLIC HEARING

Date/Time:   8/6/2026 6:00 PM

GRANTSVILLE CITY
NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
FISCAL YEAR 2027 COMPENSATION SCHEDULE


PUBLIC NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Grantsville City Council will hold a Public Hearing on Wednesday, June 17, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of receiving public input regarding the proposed Fiscal Year 2027 Compensation Schedule for Grantsville City Department Heads and Elected Officials.

The Grantsville City Council will also consider adoption of Resolution No. 2026-46 approving and adopting the Fiscal Year 2027 Compensation Schedule for Grantsville City Department Heads and Elected Officials.

The public hearing will be held in person at Grantsville City Hall, located at 429 E. Main Street, Grantsville, Utah 84029, and electronically via Zoom.

Public comments are welcome and may be provided in person during the meeting, or electronically using the following information:
Meeting URL: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/4358843411
Dial-In: 1-253-215-8782
Meeting ID: 435 884 3411

Written comments may also be submitted to the City Recorder, Alicia Fairbourne, at afairbourne@grantsvilleut.gov. All written comments will be distributed to the City Council and entered into the public record. To ensure consideration, written comments must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) on the day of the meeting.

Copies of the proposed Fiscal Year 2027 Compensation Schedule and Resolution No. 2026-46 may be reviewed during regular business hours at Grantsville City Hall or online at the Grantsville City website and the Utah Public Notice Website.


DATED this 10th day of June, 2026.
Alicia Fairbourne
Grantsville City Recorder

NOTICE OF ORDINANCE ADOPTION

PUBLIC NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that at the regular Grantsville City Council Meeting held on July 15, 2026, the Grantsville City Council adopted Ordinance 2026-26, which amends Chapter 7 of the Grantsville City Code relating to the City's Cross Connection Control Program by updating definitions, adding a definition for Dual Source Connection, and requiring reduced pressure principle assemblies for dual source connections. The ordinance also requires the removal of any noncompliant dual source connections to protect the public water system from potential contamination.

Complete copies of the adopted ordinances are available for review at the Grantsville City Recorder's office during regular business hours and online through the City's website at https://grantsville.municipalcodeonline.com/book?type=orddoc#name=2026 and the Utah Public Notice Website at https://www.utah.gov/pmn/sitemap/publicbody/1840.html.

Alicia Fairbourne
Grantsville City Recorder

title: Notice of Proposed Tax Increase and Public Hearing
agenda_text:
NOTICE OF PROPOSED TAX INCREASE
GRANTSVILLE CITY

     Grantsville City is proposing to increase its property tax revenue.

     The Grantsville City tax on a 563,000 residence would increase from $438.77 to $460.76, which is $21.99 per year.

     The Grantsville City tax on a 563,000 business would increase from $797.77 to $837.74, which is $39.97 per year.

     If the proposed budget is approved, Grantsville City would receive an additional $110,832 in property tax revenue per year as a result of the tax increase.

     If the proposed budget is approved, Grantsville City would increase its property tax budgeted revenue by 4.98% above last year's property tax budgeted revenue excluding eligible new growth.

     Grantsville City invites all concerned citizens to a public hearing for the purpose of hearing comments regarding the proposed tax increase and to explain the reasons for the proposed tax increase. You have the option to participate in the public hearing in person or virtually.


PUBLIC HEARING

     Date/Time:     Wednesday, August 5, 2026   7:00 PM MST
     Location:        Grantsville City Hall
                              429 East Main Street
                             Grantsville, UT 84029
     
To obtain more information regarding the tax increase, citizens may contact Grantsville City at 435-884-3411 or visit www.grantsvilleut.gov. NOTICE OF PROPOSED TAX INCREASE
CITY OF SARATOGA SPRINGS

The CITY OF SARATOGA SPRINGS is proposing to increase its property tax revenue. 

The CITY OF SARATOGA SPRINGS tax on a $542,000 residence would increase from $291.54 to $437.31, which is $145.77 per year.

The CITY OF SARATOGA SPRINGS tax on a $542,000 business would increase from $530.08 to $795.11, which is $265.03 per year.

If the proposed budget is approved, CITY OF SARATOGA SPRINGS would receive an additional $3,100,000 in property tax revenue per year as a result of the tax increase.

If the proposed budget is approved, CITY OF SARATOGA SPRINGS would increase its property tax budgeted revenue by 50.03% above last year's property tax budgeted revenue excluding eligible new growth.

The CITY OF SARATOGA SPRINGS invites all concerned citizens to a public hearing for the purpose of hearing comments regarding the proposed tax increase and to explain the reasons for the proposed tax increase. title: Spanish Fork City Council Notice to Spanish Fork City Utility Customers 2027
agenda_text:
NOTICE TO SPANISH FORK CITY UTILITY CUSTOMERS

State law requires that the City provide an annual disclosure on funds transferred from a utility enterprise fund to any other fund. The City has budgeted the following transfers. 

The City of Spanish Fork has budgeted for the transfer from each utility fund to the general fund as a dividend to Spanish Fork taxpayers. This dividend is the result of the rate payers' investment in the City's utility infrastructure. These funds are used each year to help cover costs of important city services like police, fire, library, senior center, parks and recreation, and other city functions. The utility transfer helps keep property taxes low in Spanish Fork. If City utility services were provided by private utility vendors, these dividends would instead be paid to the private investor-owners. Because Spanish Fork residents are the investor-owners, these dividends are used to offset what otherwise would be a significant increase in property tax rates. These transfers are of funds which cannot be defined as a reasonable allocation of costs between funds. These amounts will not be repaid. 

The amounts of the transfers are as follows:	Dollar Amount          	% of Expenditures 
From the Power Fund to the General Fund	$ 1,310,000	  3.3 % From the Water Fund to the General Fund 	$ 352,000		2.6 % 
From the Sewer Fund to the General Fund	$ 152,000	0.9 %
From the Solid Waste Fund to the General Fund 	$ 50,000 	 1.3 % 
From the Broadband Fund to the General Fund 	$ 633,171 	  5.7 % 

Spanish Fork City also has a debt obligation that the Power Fund is helping make payments on. The funds are to pay for the Justice Center (Police/Court Building). NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING AND PROPOSED ORDINANCE AMENDING CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS

SPANISH FORK CITY

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Spanish Fork City Council will hold a public hearing and consider adoption of an ordinance amending the City's Construction Standards during its regular meeting on Tuesday, June 16, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. at Spanish Fork City Hall, 80 South Main Street, Spanish Fork, Utah.

The proposed amendments to the Construction Standards include the following:

- Addition of a section for boring inspections and testing.
- Modifications to communication plan requirements for excavation permits.
- Modifications to 5-foot sewer manhole requirements.
- Addition of a section establishing the minimum depth of sewer mains.
- Clarification that inlets are not permitted within driveway access areas.
- Modifications to electrical standards.
- Modifications to water standard drawings.
- Modifications to mow strip, curb wall, and tree planting standard drawings.
- Addition of 2-inch and 3-inch PI Filter standard drawings.
- Modifications to Power & Light standard drawings.

The purpose of these amendments is to update and clarify engineering, utility, construction, and infrastructure standards applicable to public improvements and development within Spanish Fork City.

Interested persons are invited to attend the public hearing and provide comments regarding the proposed ordinance. Copies of the proposed amendments are available for public inspection at the Spanish Fork City Engineering Department during regular business hours or call 801-804-4543.

Published this 2 day of June, 2026.

Spanish Fork City

City Recorder

title: Notice of Proposed Tax Increase and Public Hearing
agenda_text:
NOTICE OF PROPOSED TAX INCREASE
TOOELE CITY

The TOOELE CITY is proposing to increase its property tax revenue.

The TOOELE CITY tax on a $410,000 residence would increase from $569.84 to $584.05, which is $14.21 per year.

The TOOELE CITY tax on a $410,000 business would increase from $1,036.07 to $1,061.90, which is $25.83 per year.

If the proposed budget is approved, TOOELE CITY would receive an additional $238,092 in property tax revenue per year as a result of the tax increase. If the proposed budget is approved, TOOELE CITY would increase its property tax budgeted revenue by 2.49% above last year's property tax budgeted revenue excluding eligible new growth.

The TOOELE CITY invites all concerned citizens to a public hearing for the purpose of hearing comments regarding the proposed tax increase and to explain the reasons for the proposed tax increase. You have the option to attend or participate in the public hearing in person or virtually.

PUBLIC HEARING
Date/Time:  8/19/2026 7:00 PM
Location:  Tooele City Hall Council Chambers, 90 North Main Street, Tooele, UT 84074

To obtain more information regarding the tax increase, citizens may contact the TOOELE CITY at 435-843-2156 or visit www.tooelecity.gov. Instructions for virtual participation in the public hearing will be available at www.tooelecity.gov no later than 24 hours before the public hearing is scheduled to begin.

Contact Person: 	Anthony Fletcher, Long Range Planner
707 E Mill Road
Suite 202
Vineyard, UT 84059
(801) 226-1929

NOTICE is hereby given regarding public hearing(s) before the City Council on June 9th, 2026, at 6 pm or as soon thereafter as possible in the council chambers at 125 S. Main Street, Vineyard, Utah 84059.

Holdaway Fields Development Agreement Amendment

The developer of Holdaway Fields has submitted a proposed amendment to the existing Development Agreement. The intent of this amendment is to align the agreement more closely with their current build strategy and implementation schedule. The proposal introduces the phasing plan, park dedication timing, and other amenities. Lot frontage standards. 

Staff reviewed the proposed amendment requests and recommends that the impact fee; including clear language that delineates city impact fees and  pass through fees for all buildings in the development be assessed and calculated at the time of building permit application, which is standard practice for cities. Impact fees should not be locked in or tied in at the time of executing the amended development agreement for any building as this will create negative fiscal impacts on other Vineyard residents and future infrastructure funding.

Public comments, questions, and requests for copies of materials are encouraged to be emailed to Anthony Fletcher at anthony@vineyardutah.gov prior to the meeting.

I, the undersigned, hereby certify that the foregoing Public Hearing Notice was posted at the Vineyard City Offices, the Vineyard City website, posted on the Utah Public Notice website, and delivered to surrounding entities.


/s/ Anthony Fletcher, Long Range Planner
